evidence: Plaut. Am. 769: Vīn' prōferrī pateram? — Prōferrī volō.
Cic. Rosc. Com. 29: ex arcā (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Of bringing a thing out from where it was kept or hidden, to show it: a letter, a witness, money from a chest.

terms.gloss: take out, bring out (from a store)
evidence: Plaut. Mil. 829: prōmpsistī tū illī vīnum?
Mart. 1.55.10: flāvaque dē rubrō prōmere mella cadō
terms.comment: Of wine from the jar, money from the treasury, books from the shelf.

phrases.latin: at ille prōfert ipsum porcellum ē sinū
phrases.english: but he produces the piglet itself from under his cloak

phrases.latin: flāvaque dē rubrō prōmere mella cadō
phrases.english: and to bring out golden honey from the red jar

phrases.latin: Cito prōferte stolam prīmam, et induite illum
phrases.english: Quick, bring out the best robe, and put it on him
